On your own computer, and nowhere else. Biryar is a program you run
yourself. There is no Biryar server, so there is nowhere for your sales
figures, your costs or your Amazon keys to go.

## What is kept, and where

Everything Biryar knows about your business is in its database, on the
computer it is installed on: your sales and fees, your buy prices, the
deals it found, every repricing decision, your settings.

Your Amazon keys, and the Keepa and ScraperAPI keys you add, are locked
with a **sealing key** before they are stored. The sealing key is made on
your computer the first time Biryar starts, and only that computer has it.
A copy of the database without the sealing key is not a pile of working
passwords: the keys in it cannot be read.

Once saved, a key is never shown again. Not on the screen, not in a log,
not to you.

## Who Biryar talks to

| | What for |
|---|---|
| Amazon | To read your own seller account, and, if you switch it on, to send a price. |
| Keepa | To look up what a barcode sells for on Amazon. |
| Your retailers' shops | To read their public product pages. |
| ScraperAPI | To read the shops that only answer a scraping service, if you add a key. |

And nothing else. In particular, **nothing is sent to us**. There is no
account with Ciya Labs, no usage reporting and no upload. A licence is
checked on your own computer, by its signature, so Biryar keeps working
without a connection to us.

## Who can get in

**A password and a code from your phone.** Signing in takes both. Someone
who learns your password still cannot get in without your phone. This is
not optional, because Biryar holds the keys to your Amazon account.

**Owners and assistants.** An owner can do everything, including what
changes money: sending prices, adding keys, inviting people. An assistant
can see everything and prepare work, and cannot do those things. Owners
invite people under **Settings, Team**.

**The computer itself.** Anyone who can sit at the computer Biryar runs on
can reach what it stores, so give that computer a password of its own.

## Keeping a copy safe

Two things make a complete backup: the database and the sealing key. The
[install guide](/setup/install/#backing-up) has the two commands. Keep
the copy somewhere that is not the same computer.

## What a shop sees

When Biryar reads a shop it says who it is, follows the shop's rules for
programs, and reads public pages only. The requests come from your own
computer, for the shops you chose. See
<https://biryar.ciyalabs.com/bot/>.

## For the technically minded

Each business's records are kept apart inside the database by PostgreSQL
itself, not by the program remembering to filter.
[How businesses are kept apart](/architecture/tenancy/) explains it for
developers.
